title.narrative: Republic of Congo Third Fiscal Management and Inclusive Growth DPF

description.narrative: The Program Development Objective is to support the government's efforts to: (i) strengthen revenue mobilization and public financial management; and (ii) improve the conditions for inclusive and sustainable growth.

The objective of the Third Fiscal Management and Inclusive Growth Development Policy Financing Program is to support the government's efforts to: (i) strengthen revenue mobilization and public financial management; and (ii) improve the conditions for inclusive and sustainable growth. This Third Fiscal Management and Inclusive Growth Development Policy Financing (DPF) is the final operation in a programmatic series and will be financed by an IDA credit of 61.1 million dollars equivalent and an IBRD loan of 18.9 million dollars. It supports the government's efforts to strengthen revenue mobilization and public financial management (PFM) and improve the conditions for inclusive and sustainable growth. The first pillar of the proposed DPF supports reforms to strengthen revenue mobilization from both the oil and non-oil sectors and PFM. The second pillar supports reforms critical for economic diversification and inclusion, including competition, business environment, human capital, protection of the most vulnerable populations, and access to electricity. The reforms supported are complementary to World Bank- Investment and Program-for-Results (PforR) operations; and build on the World Bank's core analytics, notably the recent Country Economic Memorandum, Public Finance Review, Country Climate and Development Report, and Public Expenditure and Financial Accountability assessment. The DPF series also complements the recently completed International Monetary Fund (IMF) three-year Extended Credit Facility (ECF) program.

title.narrative: RI2-A: Ordinary taxes collected from oil sector as share of oil GDP

comment.narrative: Progress toward the target indicator for this reform has been satisfactory. Ordinary taxes collected from the oil sector, as a share of oil GDP, increased from an average of 2% in 2018–2020 to 6% in 2023–2024, exceeding the 3% target.

title.narrative: RI2-B: Payout ratio from national oil company (ratio of three-year cumulative paid dividends to lagged three-year cumulative net profit)

comment.narrative: Adoption of Decree No. 2022-1857—setting rules for calculating and remitting dividends from all public enterprises, including oil—has materially boosted dividends from the main state-owned oil company. From 2022 to 2025, the average dividend payout was 33.19% of cumulative net profits, surpassing the 25% target under the DPF program

title.narrative: RI8: Reduced flaring intensity (m3 of gas flared per barrel of oil produced) back to 2017 levels by end 2025

comment.narrative: The earlier indicative action was not included in DPF3 because the Government needed additional time to conduct analysis to align the draft Gas Code with international best practices and Paris Agreement requirements; meanwhile, flaring intensity rose contrary to expectations and commitments, declining oil production that amplified intensity, potentially increasing gas-to-oil ratios in maturing fields, and insufficient interim measures to curb flaring during 2021–2024.

title.narrative: RI4: Contracts signed during the period of validity of the original bid

comment.narrative: Overall, this reform is progressing well: 54.82 percent of public contracts were signed and approved between July 2024 and June 2025 within the original bid validity. Public procurement practices show signs of increased transparency, with the share of contracts awarded through competitive procedures rising from 45 percent in 2023 to 59 percent in 2025; however, continued monitoring is warranted to confirm the durability of these gains. On this basis, the target appears achievable by June 2026.

title.narrative: RI1-B: Enrolled firms with new NIU as share of total number of firms

comment.narrative: Despite the NIU enrollment software issues late in 2025, the indicator performed strongly over the last tow year. As of December 17, 2025, 58.3 % of firms have the new NIU, well above the 25% target.

title.narrative: RI1-A: Enrolled taxpayers in e-tax with new NIU

comment.narrative: As of December 17, 2025, 48.91% of e-Tax taxpayers are enrolled with the new NIU, slightly below the DPF series target of at least 50% by June 2026. It would likely have been higher without the Q2–Q3 2025 IT software interruption that halted processing. With the old NIU scheduled for phase-out on April 1, 2026 and IT software issues being resolved, a registration surge is anticipated in early 2026, keeping the indicator on track to reach the target by June 2026.

title.narrative: Of which percentage of firms selected for tax or customs audit based on risk parameters

comment.narrative: Following the establishment of the legal and regulatory framework in 2024–2025, the authorities, with the World Bank technical assistance, plan to: (i) assess the prerequisites needed to implement risk-based audits at the General Directorate of Taxes and the General Directorate of Customs; and (ii) provide targeted training and hands-on support to staff to conduct risk-based audits and controls. This work is expected to be completed by April 2026.

title.narrative: RI6: Average disbursement rate of service delivery units operating grants (eligible primary and secondary schools, technical and vocational education and training (TVETs), and health facilities)

comment.narrative: No substantial progress in improving the efficiency of public spending in the health and education sectors due to persistent fiscal constraints. Budget appropriations available for the operation of service delivery units (schools and health centers) have remained stable, at around 13.5 percent of the total budget for education and 9.7 percent of the total budget for health, respectively. These allocations follow the formula established in Decree 2022-1875 of October 28, 2022, which introduced a formula-based resource allocation mechanism and prioritizes budget releases to basic health facilities and primary and general secondary schools. However, there are delays in the process of transferring funds to service providers. According to the Budget Directorate (DGB), in 2025, only two months of funding for the first semester (January–March) were released to frontline service providers due to fiscal constraints.

title.narrative: RI7-B: Number of female-headed households that received benefits from the national safety net program
RI7-A: Number of households that received social benefits from the national safety net program.

comment.narrative: The National Safety Net Program is operational and has provided benefits to 35,365 households, of which 24,864 are female-headed, against targets of 40,000 total households and 9,250 female-headed households by June 2026. However, the program is facing funding challenges since its launch, with no funds disbursed on the XAF12 billion allocated in 2025 in the national budget.

title.narrative: RI9: Total losses in electricity supply

comment.narrative: This earlier indicative action was not included in DPF3 because the government required additional time to undertake consultations with social partners. A letter from the Minister of Finance dated May 19, 2025, reiterated the government's commitment to finalize the reform, stating that an additional three more months are needed to advance the reform and adopt the decree delegating the management of the public electricity distribution and marketing services to the competitively selected concessionaire. The country team continues to support the reform through the Energy Investment IPF project, PASEL policy dialogue, and technical assistance.

title.narrative: RI3: Number of pilot audit reports completed by CCDB in accordance with the organic law and submitted to Parliament

comment.narrative: Although the members of the High Council of the Supreme Audit Court have been appointed, the appointment of the members of the Supreme Audit Court is still pending. There is currently no clear timeline for these appointments, making it unlikely that the results indicator will be achieved by June 2026.

title.narrative: RI5: Agencies or inspectorates with clear mandate and legal underpinnings set by new horizontal law

comment.narrative: Decree No. 2025-157list the 49 agencies and inspectorates with clear mandates and legal bases under Law No. 4-2025.

title.narrative: RI10: Number of competition policy decisions taken by the National Competition Authority and that address anticompetitive behavior and market concentration

comment.narrative: Good progress. The president of the Regulatory Authority has been appointed, as well as the central directors and the heads of service of the Regulatory Authority. The recruitment of investigators is underway. The decree establishing the Regulatory Council was adopted on November 14, 2025. The appointment of the members of the Competition Regulation Council, the last step before the operationalization of the Competition Authority, is expected by mid-January 2026. The main risk to the establishment of the Regulation Council is the political calendar. Presidential elections are scheduled for March 2026. The RI is likely to be achieved by June 2026, the target year of the reform.
